title: Expose a positive local response hidden from every finite old gradient record
statement: For any finite one-dimensional gradient-query locations and a future point xstar, including xstar among old queries, there exist C5 uniformly strongly convex potentials with identical old gradient values but different Hessians at xstar. A pointwise gradient reading at the future point is not a derivative measurement.

requires: Finite old pointwise gradient data only, with no supplied uniform higher-derivative calibration or parametric restriction ruling out the bump.
Choose positive gamma,lambda,r with lambda>1984*gamma and support avoiding other queried locations.
provides: For any finite one-dimensional gradient-query locations and a future point xstar, including xstar among old queries, there exist C5 uniformly strongly convex potentials with identical old gradient values but different Hessians at xstar. A pointwise gradient reading at the future point is not a derivative measurement.
assumptions: The derivative difference need not stay bounded away from zero under an added uniform smoothness contract. This does not contradict the separately supplied smoothness reduction.
The construction is finite-dimensional mathematical nonidentifiability, not drift, a measurement of a physical source or a general impossibility of calibrated acquisition.
costs: Additional derivative-sensitive interventions or a justified structural/smoothness promise are required; retained values alone cannot resolve this late derivative task.
contract.units: Gradient values and Hessian variation have their declared derivative units; r is input scale and gamma local curvature. Higher derivative growth scales as gamma/r^2.
contract.obstruction: Keep source-contract acquisition distinct from exploiting a supplied contract.

body: Choose r smaller than the distance to every other distinct old point. Let f(s)=s^2*(1-s^2)^6/2 on|s|<1, zero outside, Phi0(t)=lambda*t^2/2, and Phi1=Phi0+gamma*r^2*f((t-xstar)/r). Boundary derivatives through order5 vanish; fprime(0)=0 and fdoubleprime(0)=1. Old gradients agree while Hessians differ by gamma. The coefficient absolute-sum bound |fdoubleprime|<=1984 makes both strongly convex when lambda>1984*gamma>0. This is a C5 piecewise-polynomial construction, not a claim of C-infinity or global analyticity. A genuine higher-derivative promise constrains gamma/r^2 and changes the allowable ambiguity as the support shrinks; finite old records alone do not acquire that promise.
